title: Vireo after PR 169
eyebrow: Vireo engine · Windows (RTX 5060 Laptop, 8 GB) · 2026-11-15, evening · main at 7b8bd4c (PR 169 merged) · four small models at Q4 · reading, writing and first token at four prompt sizes
headline: Ahead on short prompts, level to 14% behind on long ones, behind writing after the longest
lede: Vireo's AI agent server against llama-server on the merged build, one run each, through both servers with streaming. Reading the ~32K prompt is {since:vireo|long.read_tps} faster than the afternoon's run (llama.cpp, unchanged, moved {since:llama|long.read_tps}), and Vireo is now {long.read_tps} against llama.cpp there, against {old:long.read_tps} that afternoon. At the largest prompt each model holds on this GPU (125,561 tokens for the Gemmas, 113,190 for Qwen 3.5 4B and 47,450 for Qwen 3.5 9B) Vireo reads {xlarge.read_tps} against llama.cpp and writes {xlarge.gen_tps}. On short questions Vireo answers first on all four ({short.ttft} on time to the first token), and the Gemma 4 E4B draft model keeps writing {Gemma 4 E4B|medium.gen_tps} ahead after ~3K tokens.

cards.text: Vireo reading the ~32K prompt against llama.cpp (the afternoon: {old:long.read_tps}); Vireo itself {since:vireo|long.read_tps} since then

rig.label: Software
rig.detail: main with PR 169 merged, cargo build --release · llama.cpp b12262 (CUDA build, -fa on, -ngl 99, -np 1) · vireo-server with --context and --thinking off

where: Small (a ~40-token question). Vireo ahead on first token on all four ({short.ttft}): it keeps its ~1,300-1,500 tokens of instructions from the warm-up chat and reads ~70-85 new ones. Writing level on three ({Gemma 4 E2B|short.gen_tps}, {Qwen 3.5 4B|short.gen_tps}, {Qwen 3.5 9B|short.gen_tps}) and ahead on Gemma 4 E4B ({Gemma 4 E4B|short.gen_tps}, its draft model). The reading speeds of so few tokens are mostly fixed overhead and say little.

Medium (~3K tokens). Reading level on Gemma 4 E4B ({Gemma 4 E4B|medium.read_tps}), behind on the Qwens ({Qwen 3.5 4B|medium.read_tps}, {Qwen 3.5 9B|medium.read_tps}); Gemma 4 E2B's {Gemma 4 E2B|medium.read_tps} is a one-off (drafting off it read {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo-plain|medium.read_tps}, {plain:Gemma 4 E2B|medium.read_tps} against llama.cpp, and a re-check read 18,024 and 19,150). Writing well ahead on the Gemmas ({Gemma 4 E2B|medium.gen_tps}, {Gemma 4 E4B|medium.gen_tps}, the draft models), level on the Qwens.

Large (~32K tokens). Reading behind on all four but closer than the afternoon: {Gemma 4 E4B|long.read_tps} on Gemma 4 E4B, {Gemma 4 E2B|long.read_tps} on E2B, {Qwen 3.5 4B|long.read_tps} and {Qwen 3.5 9B|long.read_tps} on the Qwens; first token the same. Writing ahead on the Gemmas ({Gemma 4 E2B|long.gen_tps}, {Gemma 4 E4B|long.gen_tps}), behind on the Qwens ({Qwen 3.5 4B|long.gen_tps}, {Qwen 3.5 9B|long.gen_tps}).

Xlarge (the largest that fits). Reading level on Qwen 3.5 4B ({Qwen 3.5 4B|xlarge.read_tps}) and Gemma 4 E4B ({Gemma 4 E4B|xlarge.read_tps}), behind on Gemma 4 E2B ({Gemma 4 E2B|xlarge.read_tps}) and Qwen 3.5 9B ({Qwen 3.5 9B|xlarge.read_tps}). Writing behind on all four ({xlarge.gen_tps}); with drafting off the Gemmas are {plain:Gemma 4 E2B|xlarge.gen_tps} and {plain:Gemma 4 E4B|xlarge.gen_tps}, so after ~125K tokens the draft models slow Vireo down rather than speed it up.
method: Small, medium and large: evals/speed/bench-2026-11-13/bench.py (the Mac's harness, Windows switches) with ENGINES=vireo,vireo-plain,llama MODELS=e2b,e4b,q4b,q9b REPS=1 WORK=short,medium,long and python -X utf8 -I, at the afternoon's contexts (65,536; 32,768 for Qwen 3.5 9B), so the change since bench-2026-11-15-windows-after-changes is the same workload. Xlarge: bench-2026-11-15-windows-after-pr169/xlarge.py, bench.py's own server classes and request with the Mac's xlarge.txt cut to fit each model's context, the same text for both engines, Windows' per-process shared GPU memory read after loading and after the prompt. Each server warmed up with a five-word chat first; one server on the GPU at a time. Speeds are the servers' own (Vireo's log, llama.cpp's timings): prompt tokens read ÷ reading time, tokens written ÷ writing time; first token is client-side. Results: results.jsonl (48 rows), xlarge.jsonl (12 rows), xlarge-probes.jsonl, recheck-e2b-medium.jsonl; page: evals/speed/bench_after_pr169_report.py.

notes.read_tps: Prompt tokens read ÷ the time reading them, as each server reports it. Vireo's small and medium prompts also carry its ~1,300 (Gemma) or ~1,480 (Qwen) tokens of instructions, kept from the warm-up chat and not read again; its large and xlarge rows keep them too since PR 169 (1,287 kept on the Gemmas' ~32K prompt, 0 that afternoon). Reading the ~32K prompt, Vireo moved {since:vireo|long.read_tps} since the afternoon and llama.cpp {since:llama|long.read_tps}.
notes.gen_tps: Vireo as shipped: the Gemmas with Google's draft models, both families with the chat's guesses. Answers differ in length between engines (the settings table has the counts), and the large and xlarge answers are short (40-70 tokens), so those writing speeds are rougher than the small and medium ones.
notes.ttft: Seconds from sending the request to the first streamed token, on the client. Shown here as llama.cpp ÷ Vireo − 1, so positive is Vireo quicker.
notes.plain: vireo-server with --mtp off --lookup 0: no draft model and no guesses, the same contexts and prompts. Bold is Vireo's writing speed with drafting off, then its difference from llama.cpp; under it, Vireo as shipped and how much drafting adds. On the Qwens there is no draft model, so the two are the same within noise.
notes.settings: Context is the --context / -c each server ran with, the same for both engines in a row; small, medium and large ran at the afternoon's contexts so they compare with it, xlarge at the largest that held. Prompt tokens are as each server counted them, with how many it kept from earlier (Vireo keeps its instructions; llama.cpp keeps its ~24-token chat start). Shared GPU memory not growing between load and after the prompt is the check that nothing spilled into the PC's memory.
notes.probes: Each model's xlarge context, found on Vireo before llama.cpp ran it. The Gemmas: 131,072 is their own largest context, and the whole of xlarge.txt (125,561 tokens on Vireo) fitted on both engines. Qwen 3.5 4B spilled at 131,072 and fitted at 98,304 and 114,688; Qwen 3.5 9B, past the 32,768 known that afternoon, fitted at 40,960 and 49,152 and spilled at 57,344. Every Vireo try is listed; a spill shows as shared memory growing and reading far below the trend of the smaller sizes.

odd: Gemma 4 E2B as shipped read the ~3K prompt at {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|medium.read_tps} tokens/s and wrote the short reply at {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|short.gen_tps}, against {old:Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|medium.read_tps} and {old:Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|short.gen_tps} that afternoon. It was the first server of the run, as it was in the afternoon's, when the same one-off happened. Re-run alone afterwards (recheck-e2b-medium.jsonl, short, medium, short, medium): 18,024 and 19,150 reading, 196.6 and 207.6 writing. The page keeps the main run's numbers.

Two xlarge tries spilled into shared GPU memory and are not used: Qwen 3.5 4B at 131,072 (read 1,199 tokens/s on 117K tokens, ~40% below the trend of 98,304 and 114,688) and Qwen 3.5 9B at 57,344 (891 tokens/s, half of 49,152's). Both showed shared memory growing 0.05 GB, with 7.6 of the 8 GB in use.

Writing after the longest prompts is slower with the Gemmas' draft models than without (Gemma 4 E2B {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|xlarge.gen_tps} against {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo-plain|xlarge.gen_tps}, E4B {Gemma 4 E4B|vireo|xlarge.gen_tps} against {Gemma 4 E4B|vireo-plain|xlarge.gen_tps}), and at ~32K on E2B the gain is small. Medium and short are where drafting pays.

Nothing errored; every row's answer is in the files. The large and xlarge answers recall one or two of the two hidden facts on both engines (the cut xlarge prompts for the Qwens may have dropped one); recall is not scored here.
